# Authentication

## Authenticating Calls

To authenticate API calls, the client must add the following header:

```javascript
Authorization: Bearer TOKEN
```

where `TOKEN` is obtained by one of the methods below.

## Token Types

There are three types of tokens which can have one of two access scopes.

| **Type** | **Scope** | |
|---|---|---|
| Personal Access Token (`PAT`) | `personal` | Generated manually from the [integrations page](https://grain.com/app/settings/account/integrations/personal_api). Doesn't expire, and can be revoked at any time. |
| Workspace Access Token (`WAT`) | `workspace` | Generated manually from the [integrations page](https://grain.com/app/settings/integrations?tab=api). Doesn't expire, and can be revoked at any time. |
| OAuth Token | `personal`, `workspace` | Issued through the OAuth2 Flow. Expires, must be refreshed. |

| **Scope** | |
|---|---|
| `personal` | Provides the same access level as the user who authorized the token. |
| `workspace` | Provides **FULL DATA ACCESS** of the workspace. Can be generated by workspace admins only. |

> **NOTE:** The `workspace` scope is not available on all plans.
> Check [https://grain.com/pricing](https://grain.com/pricing) to see if your plan includes Workspace API.

Tokens with the `personal` scope, including Personal Access Tokens, also authenticate the Grain MCP server at `https://api.grain.com/_/mcp`. Tokens with the `workspace` scope are not accepted by the MCP server.

## OAuth2 Flow

This authentication method is for developers building integrations with Grain to be used by any Grain users.

The API supports a standard OAuth2 Authorization Code flow, including the PKCE extension for client-side only authentication. At least one redirect URI is required to register a new client. For browser-based client applications, a list of CORS origins can also be added.

### Authorization Code

**Step 1**

Obtain the `client_id` and `client_secret` (only for server-side applications) credentials.

**Step 2**

Open the url `https://grain.com/_/public-api/oauth2/authorize` with the following query params.

| **Param** | |
|---|---|
| client_id | Obtained separately in **Step 1** |
| redirect_uri | Must exactly match a registered redirect URI. On `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and `[::1]`, any port matches |
| response_type | Must be `code` |
| state | Optional. Grain returns it unchanged in **Step 4**. PKCE already protects the flow, so `state` is only needed if your client relies on it |
| code_challenge | A random string, hashed with `SHA256` and `base64` URL encoded |
| code_challenge_method | Must be `S256` |
| scopes | `personal` or `workspace`. Defaults to `personal` |

**Step 3**

If the user is not already signed in to Grain, they will be prompted to sign in. After being authenticated, the user will be prompted to confirm the OAuth2 connection.

**Step 4**

The user will be redirected to `redirect_uri` from **Step 2** with the `code` query param, and `state` if you sent one.

**Step 5**

Make a `POST` request to generate the token. See [OAuth2 Generate Token](https://developers.grain.com/endpoints.html#generate-token)

**Diagram**

```
sequenceDiagram
  participant you as You
  actor user as User
  participant grain as Grain

  Note right of you: Step 1
  you-->>grain: Request Client ID & Secret (manually)
  grain-->>you: Client ID & Secret

  Note right of you: Step 2
  user->>you: Requests OAuth
  you->>user: Open or Redirects to oauth2/authorize
  user->>grain: oauth2/authorize

  Note left of grain: Step 3
  grain->>user: Requests login
  user->>grain: Login

  grain->>user: Requests Confirm OAuth
  user->>grain: Confirms

	Note left of grain: Step 4
  grain->>user: Redirects to redirect_uri w/code
  user->>you: redirect_uri w/code

  Note right of you: Step 5
  you->>grain: POST oauth2/token w/code
  grain->>you: access_token & refresh_token

  Note right of you: Refresh
  you->>grain: POST oauth2/token w/refresh_token
  grain->>you: access_token & refresh_token
```

### Client ID Metadata Document

Public clients, such as MCP clients and native apps, can skip **Step 1** by using an HTTPS URL as their `client_id`. That URL must serve a JSON [Client ID Metadata Document](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-oauth-client-id-metadata-document/) describing the client.

```json
{
  "client_id": "https://app.example.com/oauth/client.json",
  "client_name": "Example App",
  "redirect_uris": ["https://app.example.com/oauth/callback"],
  "grant_types": ["authorization_code", "refresh_token"],
  "response_types": ["code"],
  "token_endpoint_auth_method": "none"
}
```

| **Field** | |
|---|---|
| client_id | Required. Must exactly match the URL the document is served from |
| redirect_uris | Required. The `redirect_uri` in **Step 2** must exactly match one of these |
| client_name | Shown to the user when they confirm the connection. Defaults to the URL's host |
| grant_types | Must include `authorization_code`. Add `refresh_token` to receive refresh tokens |
| response_types | Must be `code` if present |
| token_endpoint_auth_method | Must be `none` if present. Client secrets are not supported |

Grain applies these rules to documents and their clients:

- The URL must use `https` and serve the document directly, with no redirects, in at most 5 KB.
- Grain caches the document for the `max-age` in its `Cache-Control` header, between 5 minutes and 24 hours, and revalidates it with its `ETag`.
- PKCE is required, so send `code_challenge` in **Step 2** and `code_verifier` when generating the token.
- `http` redirect URIs are only allowed on `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and `[::1]`, where any port matches.
- The `workspace` scope is only available to clients verified by Grain.

### Refresh Token

After the `access_token` has expired, you may generate a new one.
